newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
LALOO MOVES COURT

In a move that is bound to widen the rift in the Janata Dal party, Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav filed a petition before the Delhi High Court challenging the appointment of a returning officer and an assistant to him. He argued that there could be no legal bar on the party president from guiding the election process even though he was a candidate. The move frustrated the chances of a patch-up between Laloo and the party's working president, Sharad Yadav.
The Hindustan Times
FOUR WOMEN GET BERTH IN MINISTRY EXPANSION

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral expanded his council of ministers by inducting four women. All four will be ministers of state. The expansion was aimed at giving greater representation to women. With this expansion, the strength of Gujral's council rises to 45. Before this, there was only one woman representative in the government.
The Economic Times
FISCAL DEFICIT AT 3-3.5 PCT A PRE-REQUISITE

The committee on capital account convertibility recommended fiscal consolidation as one of the preconditions to introducing full convertibility of the rupee on the capital account. It also suggested a mandatory inflation rate for a three-year period of between three and five percent to ensure that the fiscal deficit and inflation in India are not out of line with those of major trading partners like the United States and the European Union. Too much variance would lead to the depreciation of the rupee and capital flight. The panel recommended that the fiscal deficit be reduced to three to 3.5 percent by 2000.
CONVERTIBILITY TO NECESSITATE MODIFICATION IN TAX LAWS

The move towards capital account convertibility will necessitate the amendment of Indian tax laws and tax avoidance agreements. The existing laws cannot take care of the challenges thrown up in a free regime with no restrictions on capital account convertibility, experts said.
LIST OF LOW-DUTY TELECOM IMPORTS NOTIFIED

The list of telecom equipment which will attract reduced duty has been notified by the Finance Ministry. It pegs the import duty at 20 percent and is expected to provide major relief to the private telecom companies. The notification includes a series of equipment not yet manufactured in the country such as radio communication equipment for very high and ultra high frequencies and microwave communication systems, cellular phone switches and paging control terminals.
Business Standard
DEADLINE MOOTED TO CUT BANK'S NONPERFORMING ASSETS

The Tarapore committee appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) suggested a time-bound plan to reduce the non-performing assets (NPAs) of the banking system to five percent of the total advances by 1999/2000. It also observed that financial institutions should be made to function with a targeted mandate to reduce the volume of NPAs within a time bound programme. The committee has called for measures to reduce the NPAs from the current level of 13.7 percent of the total advances. It also suggests a thorough banking law and an enforcement machinery to reduce NPAs and ensure that such a framework serves as a deterrent for future defaulters.
SAFETY BAND TO AVERT VOLATILITY IN EXCHANGE RATE MOOTED

The Tarapore committee recommended that the RBI should have a monitoring exchange-rate band of plus or minus five percent around the neutral real effective exchange rate (REER). It advised the RBI to intervene as and when the REER was outside the band. But the RBI could use its own discretion to intervene even within the band to obviate speculative forces and unwarranted volatility.
$22-31BLN FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVE ADEQUATE

The Tarapore committee reiterated the need for adequate foreign exchange reserves in a band of $22 billion to $31 billion to withstand cyclical changes in the balance of payments and unanticipated shocks which may lead to reversals of capital flows. In the absence of curbs on capital flows, four indicators were suggested: reserves should cover at least six months of imports, they should not be less than three months of imports plus half of the annual debt service payments plus one month's exports and imports, short term debt and portfolio stock should be lowered to 60 percent, the net foreign exchange assets to currency ratio should not be less than 40 percent.
CORRECTION OF I-T ANOMALY TO SPEED UP POWER PROJECTS

A major deterrent to the financial closure of the counter-guaranteed power projects has been removed with the government deciding to amend the Income Tax Act to bring the depreciation provisions in alignment with that provided under the Electricity Supply Act. Power Ministry officials said this has been endorsed by the Finance Ministry and a cabinet note will be moved to make the necessary amendment in the income tax act only with respect to power companies.
SEBI TO RECEIVE FINAL PROPOSALS ON BADLA THIS WEEK

Two committees formed by the bourse regulator, SEBI, will decide on the futures, options and the revised carry-forward (badla) system this week. The carry-forward committee has sought opinions from various regional bourses in response to the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) request for modifications in the existing badla system. The BSE president said the badla system is a time-tested instrument in the Indian bourse. The broking community feel that in the absence of a practical badla system the market will not sustain a rise. The other committee was set up to look into the implementation aspect of futures and options in the Indian bourse.
The Observer
SEBI ACT MAY BE REPLACED BY NEW ACT

In order to deal with the rise in large-scale national fraud in the capital markets and bourses, a new securities act is likely to replace the existing Securities and Exchange Board of India Act. The new act will aim at providing more teeth to the bourse regulator SEBI in the form of quasi-judicial powers or a statutory authority to enable it pay some compensation to defrauded investors and brokers.
